before: successful_flush_does_not_extend_a_pending_write failed: a successful flush erased the pending write deadline
repeated_flush_before_shutdown_keeps_the_original_deadline failed: repeated flushes kept restarting shutdown's timeout
after: Writes, flushes and shutdown retain independent deadlines with one shared lazy timer
A real Hyper connection releases a stalled shutdown after 15 seconds despite repeated polls and cancels request work
Existing progress, idle-producer, late-readiness and vectored-write regressions pass
Media URL tokens preserve 256 random bits and use URL-safe encoding without padding
Existing file Range/HEAD/revocation, pinned HTTPS bridge and live HTTP tests pass

resource_changes: No timeout allocation until an output operation first blocks; at most one timer reused per connection
Successful I/O with no pending deadline does not read the clock
Media URL tokens are encoded directly, removing two string replacements per resource
File and live resources cache the complete path instead of formatting it for each request
No new runtime dependency, thread or queue
limitations: No physical-device, CPU/RSS, end-to-end latency or two-hour soak measurements
The HTTP shutdown regression uses real Hyper with a controlled stalled transport, not a physical TLS peer
Independent AirPlay protocol code was unchanged
